Pitbulls are said to have "locking jaws". There are people who will say this isn't true, but the ones who do claim this to be true usually cite examples in which pitbulls have been tranquilized and still their jaw won't let go. A famous example was used in a court case in the US where they showed a pitbull biting down on and hanging from a cable while fully tranquilized.

Whether or not pitbulls have locking jaws is arguable, but what isn't arguable is the fact is that pitbulls have enormous bite strength, and have a hold and shake bite style. THIS IS WHY THEY'RE CONSIDERED DANGEROUS!!! Dangerous doesn't mean aggressive, it means dangerous. It's recommended that owners always have a "break stick" nearby in case an accidental bite does occur (don't use a break stick on other breeds as this can, instead of resulting in a simple bite, cause serious and more damage to whoever's being bit). A pitbull bite won't just be a simple puncture bite. The hold and shake style that pitbulls have won't end with just puncture wounds. Their bite is designed to create deep muscle damage and the tearing of tissue.

There's a saying, "It's the owner, not the dog". This is entirely true. Most pitbull owners believe they have "a dog". They don't! They have a dog with an enormous bite strength, and a hold and shake bite style. When an incident happens it's almost always the owner's fault for thinking they have a regular dog, which they don't, they have a pibull. But in the end always remember that no matter how well behaved, no matter how well trained, no matter how much of a wimp, no matter how gentle, no matter how cute, no matter how cuddly, A DOG IS A DOG. It's an animal. No matter how predictable it seems, it's still an animal. If you know that you're capable of owning a regular dog, get one. But don't get a pitbull unless you understand that it's not a regular dog and that you know for sure that you're capable of owning, and capable of controlling a pitbull in the worst circumstances. Please don't be an ignorant dog owner that ruins dog ownership for all of us.

Side note - Have you seen those clips of people putting cucumbers near cats and the cats flip out? If not google it. What that shows is that something simple can make a cat flip out and trigger its fight or flight defenses. In these cases it's flight. The cat is an animal, just like a dog is an animal. No matter how calm and well trained it is it still has triggers just like that. Instinctive triggers that will set it off without a good reason, because it's an animal. If a dog misinterprets something it sees out of the corner of its eye as a threat, it will instinctively go into fight mode. Not because it's trained to, but because of instincts. This isn't something you can un-train in a dog, this is instincts. Always remember that no matter how well you've trained or how well you think you know your dog, it's an animal.
